sentiment.model: fine-tuned RoBERTa (en) / XLM-R (other languages), int8 ONNX

negative_keywords.method: share of negative reviews mentioning each aspect phrase, kept when higher than in the other reviews; counts only, no significance test

distinctive_terms.method: Fightin' Words (Monroe et al. 2008), informative Dirichlet prior from 14 other productivity apps + this corpus; document-level counts; generic sentiment and filler words removed

drivers.method: L2 logistic regression, 1-2 vs 4-5 stars, aspect n-grams; C by 5-fold CV; 200 bootstraps, sign stability >= 0.9

complaint.name: iPhone / mobile app experience
complaint.definition: The iPhone or mobile app is worse than desktop: missing settings or features on mobile, mobile-only bugs, poor mobile usability. Not iPad-specific.

recommendations.evidence: 12% of reviews (95% CI 9%–17%); reviews mentioning it average 2.1★, 1.1★ below the rest
recommendations.action: Close the mobile-desktop gap: bring the most-missed settings and features to iPhone and fix mobile-only bugs before adding new features.

recommendations.name: Updates & compatibility
recommendations.evidence: 9% of reviews (95% CI 7%–13%); reviews mentioning it average 1.8★, 1.4★ below the rest
recommendations.action: Protect users from regressions: staged rollouts with regression checks, and avoid dropping OS versions without notice.

recommendations.evidence: 9% of reviews (95% CI 6%–13%); reviews mentioning it average 1.7★, 1.5★ below the rest
recommendations.action: Give users control over AI: an off switch or a quieter AI entry point, and keep core note-taking free of AI clutter.

quotes.text: One thing I don't love about the app is the recent addition of generative AI, but I just try to avoid using those features.

recommendations.evidence: 13% of reviews (95% CI 10%–17%); reviews mentioning it average 2.2★, 1.0★ below the rest
recommendations.action: Prioritise crash/freeze fixes: triage crash reports by device and OS, add a stability gate to releases, and target long pages and large workspaces first.
